name: Airbnb
foundedNote: Airbnb, Inc. "was incorporated in Delaware in June 2008", stated verbatim in the audited financial statements of the S-1/A. The commonly told founding story starts earlier — Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia rented air mattresses during a San Francisco design conference in October 2007, and AirBed & Breakfast launched in August 2008 — but no day-level incorporation date is given in the filing, so this is dated to the month.

public.sharesNote: Airbnb is a multi-class filer (Class A/B/C/H) and tags its cover-page count with a share-class axis, so neither dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding nor us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding is exposed by the SEC companyfacts API. The cascade falls through to us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic, which averages over the quarter rather than counting on the day, so every public point is marked soft.

regressions.note: Checked against stockanalysis.com's $82.29B. The pipeline computes $82.93B (611,000,000 weighted-average basic shares, the Q3 2025 figure, times the $135.72 close) and companiesmarketcap publishes $83.76B — a three-way spread of 1.8%, consistent with Airbnb steadily retiring stock and with the weighted-average lag described in sharesNote. The tolerance covers that spread; it is not slack.

events.note: Below the inclusion floor: an accelerator, not a round led by a named venture firm. Recorded because it is the start of the funding history, never plotted.

First round led by a named venture firm, so it clears the inclusion floor — but no post-money was ever disclosed, so it is recorded without a valuation and not plotted. Youniversity Ventures partners Jawed Karim, Keith Rabois and Kevin Hartz participated.

Greylock Partners and Sequoia Capital. Widely reported at about $7.2M, but the figure is truncated in the source consulted and no primary filing was located, so the amount is left null rather than guessed.

Andreessen Horowitz with Digital Sky Technologies, General Catalyst, and A Grade Investments (Ashton Kutcher and Guy Oseary). The $1.3B valuation attached to this round in secondary accounts could not be traced to a primary document or a fetchable contemporaneous report, so it is not recorded.
Dated to the Series C Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement of 2012-12-05, named in the S-1. Neither amount nor valuation was located in a primary or fetchable source.
Soft: the $10B is a secondary-source figure and the pre/post basis is not stated anywhere located.

General Atlantic with Hillhouse, Tiger Management, Kleiner Perkins, GGV, China Broadband Capital and Horizons Ventures. Widely reported at about $1.5B raised on a $25.5B valuation, but the amount is truncated in the source consulted and the valuation could not be confirmed, so neither is recorded.

Google Capital and Technology Crossover Ventures. Reported around $555M; the figure is truncated in the source consulted and is not recorded. The Series D/E/F Founder Voting Agreement is dated 2016-07-28 in the S-1, which brackets the series.
Brought total funding raised above $3B. Soft: secondary source, basis unstated, and no lead is named in what was located.

events.lead: Silver Lake and Sixth Street Partners
events.note: Recorded but never plotted, and the reason is a correction worth stating. This is universally described as an equity down round at an $18B valuation, but Airbnb's own S-1 says it raised '$2.0 billion in the form of term loans in April 2020'. It was debt at 9-11% interest with warrants attached, and the $18B is the warrant strike — a price at which nobody bought equity. Per the sourcing policy a primary filing beats a secondary account, and per the plotting policy a valuation nobody transacted at is never a vertex. Recorded under the terminated_deal kind because no other kind fits a debt facility; the schema has no debt category, which is itself a limitation worth noting.

curatorNotes: This shard is deliberately sparse where the sourcing was. Two prior research agents died to API errors before writing it and a third stalled, so it was completed by hand under time pressure, and the honest consequence is that only two pre-IPO rounds carry a plotted valuation — the 2014 Series D at $10B and the 2017 round at $31B — both soft. Airbnb's S-1 preferred-stock note certainly contains the full cap table with per-share issue prices, which would price every series properly; it resisted text extraction from the 5MB filing and was not recovered. Anyone revisiting this file should start there. What IS primary here: the June 2008 Delaware incorporation, the Series B and Series C purchase-agreement dates, the Series D/E/F Founder Voting Agreement date, and the characterisation of the April 2020 financing as term loans rather than equity.
unresolved: Per-share issue prices and post-money valuations for Series A, B, C, E and F — recoverable from the S-1 preferred-stock note, which was not successfully parsed.
Amounts raised in the Series A, E and F rounds; every figure available was truncated in the source consulted and none was confirmed against a filing.
The $1.3B valuation widely attached to the 2011 Series B could not be traced to any primary or fetchable contemporaneous source.

Whether any part of the April 2020 Silver Lake / Sixth Street financing was genuinely equity. The S-1 describes $2.0B of term loans; secondary accounts describe $1B of shares at $18B plus $1B of debt. The filing was followed.
